one_liner: Senior TSA contract specialist (GS-14 equivalent) in Springfield who plans major acquisitions, runs contract administration, interprets procurement policy and mentors junior contracting staff.
fit_summary: This senior 1102 role requires four years of contracting, a year directing contract administration (modifications, claims, performance appraisals), 24 business-related semester hours and FAC-C (Professional) certification. Daniel's procurement work is contractor-side proposals and medical-supply purchasing at IEM, with no FAC-C or contract administration, so he would be rated ineligible.
eligibility: Open to the public under Direct Hire Authority, so no federal status or veterans' preference is needed.

You need one year of specialized experience at SV-I/GS-13 level covering all four areas: full-range contract administration, interpreting complex contracting policy, major acquisition planning, and mentoring others in contract execution. You also need four years of progressively responsible contracting experience.

You need a bachelor's degree that includes at least 24 semester hours in accounting, business, finance, law, contracts, purchasing, economics, management or similar fields, and you must submit transcripts by the closing date.
FAC-C (Professional) certification or equivalent must be verified.
You must obtain a Secret clearance and a favorable background investigation, file a financial disclosure, be a U.S. citizen, and be registered with Selective Service.
strategy: Skip this one: it requires a year directing contract administration and FAC-C (Professional) certification, and his resume shows neither.

If contracting interests him, GS-1102 contract specialist postings at GS-7/9 that are open to the public are the realistic entry point; otherwise, FEMA or Virginia VDEM emergency management roles fit his IEM background.
resume_bullets: Found multimillion-dollar opportunities in SAM.gov, GovWin and the DHS acquisition forecast, and led proposal writing (2019–2024).
Procured supplies and set up vendor relationships for COVID-19 sites in six states (2021–2022).
interview_questions: Walk us through how you handled a contract claim or dispute from start to finish.
How have you planned a major acquisition so it met timeliness and functionality needs?
Tell us about a time you interpreted an ambiguous contracting policy and developed a new approach.
How do you coach less-experienced specialists or CORs to improve their performance?
watch_outs: The contract administration experience, business coursework and FAC-C requirements are strict, and his resume shows none of them.
The role requires a Secret clearance and financial disclosure.
